business_problem: MUSINSA, an online fashion platform in Korea with 13 million subscribers, recently underwent rapid growth in various aspects of its business, including new subscribers, sales, and the number of brands on its site. As a result, the business faced increased data and complexity, prompting the implementation of the Databricks Data + AI Platform to address diverse data needs arising from this increase.
solution_summary: MUSINSA, an online fashion platform in Korea with 13 million subscribers, recently underwent rapid growth in various aspects of its business, including new subscribers, sales, and the number of brands on its site. As a result, the business faced increased data and complexity, prompting the implementation of the Databricks Data + AI Platform to address diverse data needs arising from this increase. With consumer and sales data at its fingertips, it can make smarter decisions, introduce recommendation services, and streamline operations to maintain its position as the No. 1 fashion store in Korea. To provide nearly 1,500 employees with a more accessible data environment catering to their varying levels of data usage and work requirements, MUSINSA implemented Databricks Data + AI Platform as the centralized platform to store, understand and analyze all data types.

solution_components.name: Databricks Data + AI Platform
solution_components.role: Provides the shared lakehouse environment for ingestion, engineering, analytics, and AI workloads.

solution_components.name: Unity Catalog
solution_components.role: Applies centralized governance, lineage, and access controls across shared data assets.

solution_components.name: Databricks SQL
solution_components.role: Serves dashboards, self-service queries, and business intelligence for downstream users.

data_flow: Customer, product, and engagement data lands in Databricks, is transformed in the lakehouse under Unity Catalog governance, and is served to downstream users and applications through Databricks SQL.
business_outcome: Reported outcomes include 1,500 Employees can access and share data for internal decision-making; 40%-60% Yearly increase in data volume supported.
